studies.title: Stop, Then Spread Out
studies.meaning: The instruction is bounded on both sides. Business stops at the call and resumes when the prayer ends, and the second ayah is as explicit as the first about the resumption. Scholars differ over whether the word for hastening means physical speed or serious attention, and most take the second, since walking calmly is reported elsewhere. What the pair establishes is an interruption with a defined edge, not a withdrawal from work.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan. The gathering had been held in Medina from early in the settlement, and the surah takes its name from the day. The last ayah of the surah records an occasion the sources report with reasonable agreement: a trading caravan arrived while the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was addressing the congregation, and much of it left to meet the caravan. The instruction here is read against that.

keyTerms.note: The same verb the Quran uses for striving in general. Classical readers stress it does not mean running, and an early reading of the word as walking is transmitted, so the urgency is of intention rather than pace.
The specific word for a completed sale rather than for work in general. Naming the transaction rather than the trade keeps the pause narrow: what stops is the deal in progress.
A verb of dispersal used of people spreading across ground and of things being unfurled. It sends the congregation outward as deliberately as the first ayah gathered it in.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Medina's market was open ground with no permanent stalls, and a caravan's arrival was the event of the season. Grain, cloth and oil came in from Syria on a schedule nobody controlled, and prices moved in the first hour. Missing that hour cost money. The two ayat land on people for whom stopping a sale halfway was a real loss, and the second ayah gives them their afternoon back.
studies.didYouKnow: The word for the day appears only once in the whole Quran, in this ayah, and it is the source of the modern Arabic name for Friday. Early sources record that the Arabs had called the day something else before, and that the name in use now comes from the gathering rather than the gathering from the name.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The passage arranges a week rather than restricting one. Commerce is not treated as a rival to worship; it is stopped for a defined interval and then commanded to resume, in the imperative, using the same grammatical form as the instruction to pray. That places earning inside the religious frame rather than outside it. The remembrance asked for in the second ayah is then attached to the dispersal, not to the gathering.

crossReferences.why: Records the incident the whole passage is usually read against, a congregation leaving for a caravan.
Names the people this instruction produces, traders whose business does not pull them away from remembrance.
Makes the same point in another setting, allowing trade inside a season set aside for worship.

studies.applyIt: Put a hard edge on one interruption this week. Choose a fixed time, close whatever you are doing mid-sentence, and give twenty minutes to something with no output. Then go straight back. The passage is not asking for less work; it is asking whether anything in your week is capable of stopping you.
